data/definitions/01/greek.description: α΄. Δεδομένα τῷ μεγέθει λέγεται χωρία τε καὶ γραμμαὶ καὶ γωνίαι, οἷς δυνάμεθα ἴσα πορίσασθαι.

data/definitions/01/index.title: Definition 1 [α΄ · Def. I]: Given in Magnitude
data/definitions/01/index.description: Spaces, lines, and angles are called given in magnitude to which we can procure equals.

data/definitions/02/greek.title: Ὅρος β΄ [D.def.2]
data/definitions/02/greek.description: β΄. Λόγος δεδόσθαι λέγεται, ᾧ δυνάμεθα τὸν αὐτὸν πορίσασθαι.

data/definitions/02/index.title: Definition 2 [β΄ · Def. II]: Given in Ratio
data/definitions/02/index.description: A ratio is said to be given to which we can procure an identical ratio.

data/definitions/03/greek.title: Ὅρος γ΄ [D.def.3]
data/definitions/03/greek.description: γ΄. Εὐθύγραμμα σχήματα τῷ εἴδει δεδόσθαι λέγεται, ὧν αἵ τε γωνίαι δεδομέναι εἰσὶ κατὰ μίαν καὶ οἱ λόγοι τῶν πλευρῶν πρὸς ἀλλήλας δεδομένοι.

data/definitions/03/index.title: Definition 3 [γ΄ · Def. III]: Given in Species
data/definitions/03/index.description: Rectilineal figures are said to be given in species whose angles are severally given and the ratios of whose sides to one another are given.

data/definitions/04/greek.title: Ὅρος δ΄ [D.def.4]
data/definitions/04/greek.description: δ΄. Τῇ θέσει δεδόσθαι λέγονται σημεῖά τε καὶ γραμμαὶ καὶ γωνίαι, ἃ τὸν αὐτὸν ἀεὶ τόπον ἐπέχει.

data/definitions/04/index.title: Definition 4 [δ΄ · Def. IV (cf. Def. A)]: Given in Position
data/definitions/04/index.description: Points, lines, and angles are said to be given in position which always occupy the same place.

data/definitions/05/greek.title: Ὅρος ε΄ [D.def.5]
data/definitions/05/greek.description: ε΄. Κύκλος τῷ μεγέθει δεδόσθαι λέγεται, οὗ δέδοται ἡ ἐκ τοῦ κέντρου τῷ μεγέθει.

data/definitions/05/index.title: Definition 5 [ε΄ · Def. V]: Circle Given in Magnitude
data/definitions/05/index.description: A circle is said to be given in magnitude whose radius (straight line from the centre) is given in magnitude.

data/definitions/06/greek.description: ϛ΄. Τῇ θέσει δὲ καὶ τῷ μεγέθει κύκλος δεδόσθαι λέγεται, οὗ δέδοται τὸ μὲν κέντρον τῇ θέσει, ἡ δὲ ἐκ τοῦ κέντρου τῷ μεγέθει.

data/definitions/06/index.title: Definition 6 [ϛ΄ · Def. VI]: Circle Given in Position & Magnitude
data/definitions/06/index.description: A circle is said to be given in position and in magnitude whose centre is given in position and whose radius is given in magnitude.

data/definitions/07/greek.description: ζ΄. Τμήματα κύκλων τῷ μεγέθει δεδόσθαι λέγεται, ἐν οἷς αἱ γωνίαι δεδομέναι εἰσὶ καὶ αἱ βάσεις τῶν τμημάτων τῷ μεγέθει.

data/definitions/07/index.title: Definition 7 [ζ΄ · Def. VII]: Segment Given in Magnitude
data/definitions/07/index.description: Segments of circles are said to be given in magnitude in which the inscribed angles are given and the bases of the segments are given in magnitude.

data/definitions/08/greek.title: Ὅρος η΄ [D.def.8]
data/definitions/08/greek.description: η΄. Τῇ θέσει δὲ καὶ τῷ μεγέθει τμήματα δεδόσθαι λέγεται, ἐν οἷς αἵ τε γωνίαι δεδομέναι εἰσὶ τῷ [p.4] μεγέθει καὶ αἱ βάσεις τῶν τμημάτων τῇ θέσει καὶ τῷ μεγέθει.

data/definitions/08/index.title: Definition 8 [η΄ · Def. VIII]: Segment Given in Position & Magnitude
data/definitions/08/index.description: Segments of circles are said to be given in position and in magnitude in which the inscribed angles are given in magnitude and the bases of the segments are given in position and in magnitude.

data/definitions/09/greek.title: Ὅρος θ΄ [D.def.9]
data/definitions/09/greek.description: θ΄. Μέγεθος μεγέθους δοθέντι μεῖζόν ἐστιν, ὅταν, ἀφαιρεθέντος τοῦ δοθέντος, τὸ λοιπὸν τῷ αὐτῷ ἴσον ᾖ.

data/definitions/09/index.title: Definition 9 [θ΄ · Def. IX]: Affine Excess (δοθέντι μεῖζον)
data/definitions/09/index.description: A magnitude is greater than a magnitude by a given magnitude when, the given magnitude being subtracted, the remainder is equal to that same magnitude.

data/definitions/10/greek.description: ι΄. Μέγεθος μεγέθους δοθέντι ἔλασσόν ἐστιν, ὅταν, προστεθέντος τοῦ δοθέντος, τὸ ὅλον τῷ αὐτῷ ἴσον ᾖ.

data/propositions/01/greek.title: Πρότασις α΄ [D.1 · Prop. Prop. I]
data/propositions/01/greek.description: Τῶν δεδομένων μεγεθῶν ὁ λόγος ὁ πρὸς ἄλληλα δέδοται.

data/propositions/01/index.title: Proposition 1 [α΄ · Prop. Prop. I]
data/propositions/01/index.description: The ratio of given magnitudes to one another is given.

data/propositions/01/notes.title: Proposition 1 — Philological & Critical Notes
data/propositions/01/notes.description: D.1 (Prop. I) — Elements G-Index: G.183, G.195 · Pappus: Synagoge VII.3

data/propositions/02/greek.title: Πρότασις β΄ [D.2 · Prop. Prop. II]
data/propositions/02/greek.description: Ἐὰν δεδομένον μέγεθος πρὸς ἄλλο τι μέγεθος λόγον ἔχῃ δεδομένον, δέδοται κᾀκεῖνο τῷ μεγέθει.

data/propositions/02/index.title: Proposition 2 [β΄ · Prop. Prop. II]
data/propositions/02/index.description: If a given magnitude have a given ratio to some other magnitude, that other is also given in magnitude.

data/propositions/02/notes.title: Proposition 2 — Philological & Critical Notes
data/propositions/02/notes.description: D.2 (Prop. II) — Elements G-Index: G.189, G.187, G.222 · Pappus: Synagoge VII.3 · Petersen (1879): Similarity / Scaling · Altshiller-Court (1952): § 18 (Fourth Proportional)

data/propositions/03/greek.title: Πρότασις γ΄ [D.3 · Prop. Prop. III]
data/propositions/03/greek.description: Ἐὰν δεδομένα μεγέθη ὁποσαοῦν συντεθῇ, καὶ τὸ ἐξ αὐτῶν συγκείμενον δεδομένον ἔσται.

data/propositions/03/index.title: Proposition 3 [γ΄ · Prop. Prop. III]
data/propositions/03/index.description: If any multitude of given magnitudes be compounded together, the magnitude compounded out of them will also be given.

data/propositions/03/notes.title: Proposition 3 — Philological & Critical Notes
data/propositions/03/notes.description: D.3 (Prop. III) — Elements G-Index: G.36 · Petersen (1879): Algebraic Method · Altshiller-Court (1952): § 6 (Sum of Segments)

data/propositions/04/greek.title: Πρότασις δ΄ [D.4 · Prop. Prop. IV]
data/propositions/04/greek.description: Ἐὰν ἀπὸ δεδομένου μεγέθους δεδομένον μέγεθος ἀφαιρεθῇ, τὸ λοιπὸν δεδομένον ἔσται.

data/propositions/04/index.title: Proposition 4 [δ΄ · Prop. Prop. IV]
data/propositions/04/index.description: If from a given magnitude a given magnitude be subtracted, the remainder will also be given.

data/propositions/04/notes.title: Proposition 4 — Philological & Critical Notes
data/propositions/04/notes.description: D.4 (Prop. IV) — Elements G-Index: G.19 · Petersen (1879): Algebraic Method · Altshiller-Court (1952): § 6 (Difference of Segments)

data/propositions/05/greek.title: Πρότασις ε΄ [D.5 · Prop. Prop. VI]
data/propositions/05/greek.description: Ἐὰν μέγεθος πρὸς ἑαυτοῦ τι μέρος λόγον ἔχῃ δεδομένον, καὶ πρὸς τὸ λοιπὸν λόγον ἕξει δεδομένον.

data/propositions/05/index.title: Proposition 5 [ε΄ · Prop. Prop. VI]
data/propositions/05/index.description: If a magnitude have a given ratio to a part of itself, it will also have a given ratio to the remainder.

data/propositions/05/notes.title: Proposition 5 — Philological & Critical Notes
data/propositions/05/notes.description: D.5 (Prop. VI) — Elements G-Index: G.201 · Pappus: Synagoge VII.4

data/propositions/06/greek.title: Πρότασις Ϛ΄ [D.6 · Prop. Prop. VII]
data/propositions/06/greek.description: Ἐὰν δύο μεγέθη συντεθῇ πρὸς ἄλληλα λόγον ἔχοντα δεδομένον, καὶ τὸ ὅλον πρὸς ἑκάτερον αὐτῶν λόγον ἕξει δεδομένον.

data/propositions/06/index.title: Proposition 6 [Ϛ΄ · Prop. Prop. VII]

heath/volume_II/book_ix/index.title: Book IX
heath/volume_II/book_ix/index.description: Culmination of Euclidean number theory across 36 propositions: Euclid’s theorem on the infinitude of primes (IX.20), geometric series sums, and even perfect numbers (IX.36).

heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/01/.title: Proposition IX.1
heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/01/.description: If two similar plane numbers by multiplying one another make some number, the product will be square.

heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/02/.title: Proposition IX.2
heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/02/.description: If two numbers by multiplying one another make a square number, they are similar plane numbers.

heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/03/.title: Proposition IX.3
heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/03/.description: If a cube number by multiplying itself make some number, the product will be cube.

heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/04/.title: Proposition IX.4
heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/04/.description: If a cube number by multiplying a cube number make some number, the product will be cube.

heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/05/.title: Proposition IX.5
heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/05/.description: If a cube number by multiplying any number make a cube number, the multiplied number will also be cube.

heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/06/.title: Proposition IX.6
heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/06/.description: If a number by multiplying itself make a cube number, it will itself also be cube.

heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/07/.title: Proposition IX.7
heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/07/.description: If a composite number by multiplying any number make some number, the product will be solid.

heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/08/.description: If as many numbers as we please beginning from an unit be in continued proportion, the third from the unit will be square, as will also those which successively leave out one; the fourth will be cube, as will also all those which leave…

heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/09/.title: Proposition IX.9
heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/09/.description: If as many numbers as we please beginning from an unit be in continued proportion, and the number after the unit be square, all the rest will also be square. And, if the number after the unit be cube, all the rest will also be cube.

heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/10/.title: Proposition IX.10
heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/10/.description: If as many numbers as we please beginning from an unit be in continued proportion, and the number after the unit be not square, neither will any other be square except the third from the unit and all those which leave out one. And, if the…

heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/11/.title: Proposition IX.11
heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/11/.description: If as many numbers as we please beginning from an unit be in continued proportion, the less measures the greater according to some one of the numbers which have place among the proportional numbers.

heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/12/.title: Proposition IX.12
heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/12/.description: If as many numbers as we please beginning from an unit be in continued proportion, by however many prime numbers the last is measured, the next to the unit will also be measured by the same.

heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/13/.title: Proposition IX.13
heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/13/.description: If as many numbers as we please beginning from an unit be in continued proportion, and the number after the unit be prime, the greatest will not be measured by any except those which have a place among the proportional numbers.

heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/14/.title: Proposition IX.14
heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/14/.description: If a number be the least that is measured by prime numbers, it will not be measured by any other prime number except those originally measuring it.

heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/15/.title: Proposition IX.15
heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/15/.description: If three numbers in continued proportion be the least of those which have the same ratio with them, any two whatever added together will be prime to the remaining number.

heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/16/.title: Proposition IX.16
heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/16/.description: If two numbers be prime to one another, the second will not be to any other number as the first is to the second.

heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/17/.title: Proposition IX.17
heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/17/.description: If there be as many numbers as we please in continued proportion, and the extremes of them be prime to one another, the last will not be to any other number as the first to the second.

heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/18/.title: Proposition IX.18
heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/18/.description: Given two numbers, to investigate whether it is possible to find a third proportional to them.

heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/19/.title: Proposition IX.19
heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/19/.description: Given three numbers, to investigate when it is possible to find a fourth proportional to them.

heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/20/.title: Proposition IX.20
heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/20/.description: Prime numbers are more than any assigned multitude of prime numbers.

heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/21/.title: Proposition IX.21
heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/21/.description: If as many even numbers as we please be added together, the whole is even.

heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/22/.title: Proposition IX.22
heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/22/.description: If as many odd numbers as we please be added together, and their multitude be even, the whole will be even.

heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/23/.title: Proposition IX.23
heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/23/.description: If as many odd numbers as we please be added together, and their multitude be odd, the whole will also be odd.

heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/24/.title: Proposition IX.24
heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/24/.description: If from an even number an even number be subtracted, the remainder will be even.

heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/25/.title: Proposition IX.25
heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/25/.description: If from an even number an odd number be subtracted, the remainder will be odd.

heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/26/.title: Proposition IX.26
heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/26/.description: If from an odd number an odd number be subtracted, the remainder will be even.

heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/27/.title: Proposition IX.27
heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/27/.description: If from an odd number an even number be subtracted, the remainder will be odd.

heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/28/.title: Proposition IX.28
heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/28/.description: If an odd number by multiplying an even number make some number, the product will be even.

heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/29/.title: Proposition IX.29
heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/29/.description: If an odd number by multiplying an odd number make some number, the product will be odd.

heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/30/.title: Proposition IX.30
heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/30/.description: If an odd number measure an even number, it will also measure the half of it.

heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/31/.title: Proposition IX.31
heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/31/.description: If an odd number be prime to any number, it will also be prime to the double of it.

heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/32/.title: Proposition IX.32
heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/32/.description: Each of the numbers which are continually doubled beginning from a dyad is even-times even only.

heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/33/.title: Proposition IX.33
heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/33/.description: If a number have its half odd, it is even-times odd only.

heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/34/.title: Proposition IX.34
heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/34/.description: If a number neither be one of those which are continually doubled from a dyad, nor have its half odd, it is both even-times even and even-times odd.

heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/35/.description: If as many numbers as we please be in continued proportion, and there be subtracted from the second and the last numbers equal to the first, then, as the excess of the second is to the first, so will the excess of the last be to all those…

heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/36/.title: Proposition IX.36
heath/volume_II/book_ix/propositions/36/.description: If as many numbers as we please beginning from an unit be set out continuously in double proportion, until the sum of all becomes prime, and if the sum multiplied into the last make some number, the product will be perfect.

heath/volume_II/book_v/definitions/index.title: Book V Definitions
heath/volume_II/book_v/definitions/index.description: A magnitude is a part of a magnitude, the less of the greater, when it measures the greater.

heath/volume_II/book_v/index.description: Eudoxus’s general theory of ratios and proportions for commensurable and incommensurable magnitudes across 18 definitions and 25 propositions.

heath/volume_II/book_v/propositions/05/i.title: Proposition V.5
heath/volume_II/book_v/propositions/05/i.description: If a magnitude be the same multiple of a magnitude that a part subtracted is of a part subtracted, the remainder will also be the same multiple of the remainder that the whole is of the whole.

heath/volume_II/book_v/propositions/06/i.title: Proposition V.6
heath/volume_II/book_v/propositions/06/i.description: If two magnitudes be equimultiples of two magnitudes, and any magnitudes subtracted from them be equimultiples of the same, the remainders also are either equal to the same or equimultiples of them.

heath/volume_II/book_v/propositions/07/i.title: Proposition V.7
heath/volume_II/book_v/propositions/07/i.description: Equal magnitudes have to the same the same ratio, as also has the same to equal magnitudes.

heath/volume_II/book_v/propositions/08/i.title: Proposition V.8
heath/volume_II/book_v/propositions/08/i.description: Of unequal magnitudes, the greater has to the same a greater ratio than the less has; and the same has to the less a greater ratio than it has to the greater.

heath/volume_II/book_v/propositions/09/i.title: Proposition V.9
heath/volume_II/book_v/propositions/09/i.description: Magnitudes which have the same ratio to the same are equal to one another ; and magnitudes to which the same has the same ratio are equal.

heath/volume_II/book_v/propositions/10/i.title: Proposition V.10
heath/volume_II/book_v/propositions/10/i.description: Of magnitudes which have a ratio to the same, that which has a greater ratio is greater ; and that to which the same has a greater ratio is less.

heath/volume_II/book_v/propositions/11/i.title: Proposition V.11
heath/volume_II/book_v/propositions/11/i.description: Ratios which are the same with the same ratio are also the same with one another.

heath/volume_II/book_v/propositions/12/i.title: Proposition V.12
heath/volume_II/book_v/propositions/12/i.description: If any number of magnitudes be proportional, as one of the antecedents is to one of the consequents, so will all the antecedents be to all the consequents.

heath/volume_II/book_v/propositions/13/i.title: Proposition V.13
heath/volume_II/book_v/propositions/13/i.description: If a first magnitude have to a second the same ratio as a third to a fourth, and the third have to the fourth a greater ratio than a fifth has to a sixth, the first will also have to the second a greater ratio than the fifth to the sixth.

heath/volume_II/book_v/propositions/14/i.title: Proposition V.14
heath/volume_II/book_v/propositions/14/i.description: If a first magnitude have to a second the same ratio as a third has to a fourth, and the first be greater than the third, the second will also be greater than the fourth ; if equal, equal ; and if less, less.

heath/volume_II/book_v/propositions/15/i.title: Proposition V.15
heath/volume_II/book_v/propositions/15/i.description: Parts have the same ratio as the same multiples of them taken in corresponding order.

heath/volume_II/book_v/propositions/22/i.description: If there be any number of magnitudes whatever, and others equal to them in multitude, which taken two and two together are in the same ratio, they will also be in the same ratio ex aequali.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/014.title: Proposition X.14
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/014.description: If four straight lines be proportional, and the square on the first be greater than the square on the second by the square on a straight line commensurable with the first,1 the square on the third will also be greater than the square on…

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/015.title: Proposition X.15
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/015.description: If two commensurable magnitudes be added together, the whole will also be commensurable with each of them; and, if the whole be commensurable with one of them, the original magnitudes will also be commensurable.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/016.title: Proposition X.16
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/016.description: If two incommensurable magnitudes be added together, the whole will also be incommensurable with each of them; and, if the whole be incommensurable with one of them, the original magnitudes will also be incommensurable.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/018.title: Proposition X.18
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/018.description: If there be two unequal straight lines, and to the greater there be applied a parallelogram equal to the fourth part of the square on the less and deficient by a square figure, and if it divide it into parts which are incommensurable, the…

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/019.title: Proposition X.19
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/019.description: The rectangle contained by rational straight lines commensurable in length is rational.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/020.title: Proposition X.20
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/020.description: If a rational area be applied to a rational straight line, it produces as breadth a straight line rational and commensurable in length with the straight line to which it is applied.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/021.title: Proposition X.21
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/021.description: The rectangle contained by rational straight lines commensurable in square only is irrational, and the side of the square equal to it is irrational. Let the latter be called medial.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/022.title: Proposition X.22
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/022.description: The square on a medial straight line, if applied to a rational straight line, produces as breadth a straight line rational and incommensurable in length with that to which it is applied.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/023.title: Proposition X.23
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/023.description: A straight line commensurable with a medial straight line is medial.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/024.title: Proposition X.24
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/024.description: The rectangle contained by medial straight lines commensurable in length is medial.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/025.title: Proposition X.25
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/025.description: The rectangle contained by medial straight lines commensurable in square only is either rational or medial.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/026.title: Proposition X.26
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/026.description: A medial area does not exceed a medial area by a rational area.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/027.title: Proposition X.27
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/027.description: To find medial straight lines commensurable in square only which contain a rational rectangle.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/028.title: Proposition X.28
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/028.description: To find medial straight lines commensurable in square only which contain a medial rectangle.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/029.title: Proposition X.29
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/029.description: To find two rational straight lines commensurable in square only and such that the square on the greater is greater than the square on the less by the square on a straight line commensurable in length with the greater.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/030.title: Proposition X.30
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/030.description: To find two rational straight lines commensurable in square only and such that the square on the greater is greater than the square on the less by the square on a straight line incommensurable in length with the greater.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/031.title: Proposition X.31
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/031.description: To find two medial straight lines commensurable in square only, containing a rational rectangle, and such that the square on the greater is greater than the square on the less by the square on a straight line commensurable in length with…

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/032.title: Proposition X.32
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/032.description: To find two medial straight lines commensurable in square only, containing a medial rectangle, and such that the square on the greater is greater than the square on the less by the square on a straight line commensurable with the greater.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/033.title: Proposition X.33
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/033.description: To find two straight lines incommensurable in square which make the sum of the squares on them rational but the rectangle contained by them medial.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/034.title: Proposition X.34
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/034.description: To find two straight lines incommensurable in square which make the sum of the squares on them medial but the rectangle contained by them rational.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/035.title: Proposition X.35
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/035.description: To find two straight lines incommensurable in square which make the sum of the squares on them medial and the rectangle contained by them medial and moreover incommensurable with the sum of the squares on them.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/036.title: Proposition X.36
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/036.description: If two rational straight lines commensurable in square only be added together, the whole is irrational; and let it be called binomial.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/037.title: Proposition X.37
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/037.description: If two medial straight lines commensurable in square only and containing a rational rectangle be added together, the whole is irrational; and let it be called a first bimedial straight line.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/038.title: Proposition X.38
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/038.description: If two medial straight lines commensurable in square only and containing a medial rectangle be added together, the whole is irrational; and let it be called a second bimedial straight line.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/039.title: Proposition X.39
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/039.description: If two straight lines incommensurable in square which make the sum of the squares on them rational, but the rectangle contained by them medial, be added together, the whole straight line is irrational : and let it be called major.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/040.title: Proposition X.40
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/040.description: If two straight lines incommensurable in square which make the sum of the squares on them medial, but the rectangle contained by them rational, be added together, the whole straight line is irrational; and let it be called the side of a…

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/041.title: Proposition X.41
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/041.description: If two straight lines incommensurable in square which make the sum of the squares on them medial, and the rectangle contained by them medial and also incommensurable with the sum of the squares on them, be added together, the whole…

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/042.title: Proposition X.42
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/042.description: A binomial straight line is divided into its terms at one point only.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/043.title: Proposition X.43
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/043.description: A first bimedial straight line is divided at one point only.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/044.title: Proposition X.44
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/044.description: A second bimedial straight line is divided at one point only.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/045.title: Proposition X.45
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/045.description: A major straight line is divided at one and the same point only.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/046.title: Proposition X.46
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/046.description: The side of a rational plus a medial area is divided at one point only.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/047.title: Proposition X.47
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/047.description: The side of the sum of two medial areas is divided at one point only.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/048.title: Proposition X.48
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/048.description: To find the first binomial straight line.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/049.title: Proposition X.49
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/049.description: To find the second binomial straight line.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/050.title: Proposition X.50

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/051.title: Proposition X.51
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/051.description: To find the fourth binomial straight line.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/052.title: Proposition X.52
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/052.description: To find the fifth binomial straight line.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/053.title: Proposition X.53
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/053.description: To find the sixth binomial straight line.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/054.title: Proposition X.54
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/054.description: If an area be contained by a rational straight line and the first binomial, the “side”1 of the area is the irrational straight line which is called binomial.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/055.title: Proposition X.55
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/055.description: If an area be contained by a rational straight line and the second binomial, the “side” of the area is the irrational straight line which is called a first bimedial.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/056.title: Proposition X.56
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/056.description: If an area be contained by a rational straight line and the third binomial, the “side” of the area is the irrational straight line called a second bimedial.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/057.title: Proposition X.57
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/057.description: If an area be contained by a rational straight line and the fourth binomial, the “side” of the area is the irrational straight line called major.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/058.title: Proposition X.58
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/058.description: If an area be contained by a rational straight line and the fifth binomial, the “side” of the area is the irrational straight line called the side of a rational plus a medial area.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/059.title: Proposition X.59
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/059.description: If an area be contained by a rational straight line and the sixth binomial, the “side” of the area is the irrational straight line called the side of the sum of two medial areas.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/060.title: Proposition X.60
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/060.description: The square on the binomial straight line applied to a rational straight line produces as breadth the first binomial.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/061.title: Proposition X.61
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/061.description: The square on the first bimedial straight line applied to a rational straight line produces as breadth the second binomial.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/062.title: Proposition X.62
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/062.description: The square on the second bimedial straight line applied to a rational straight line produces as breadth the third binomial.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/063.title: Proposition X.63
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/063.description: The square on the major straight line applied to a rational straight line produces as breadth the fourth binomial.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/064.title: Proposition X.64
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/064.description: The square on the side of a rational plus a medial area applied to a rational straight line produces as breadth the fifth binomial.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/065.title: Proposition X.65
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/065.description: The square on the side of the sum of two medial areas applied to a rational straight line produces as breadth the sixth binomial.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/066.title: Proposition X.66
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/066.description: A straight line commensurable in length with a binomial straight line is itself also binomial and the same in order.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/067.title: Proposition X.67
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/067.description: A straight line commensurable in length with a bimedial straight line is itself also bimedial and the same in order.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/068.title: Proposition X.68
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/068.description: A straight line commensurable with a major straight line is itself also major.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/069.title: Proposition X.69
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/069.description: A straight line commensurable with the side of a rational plus a medial area is itself also the side of a rational plus a medial area.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/070.title: Proposition X.70
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/070.description: A straight line commensurable with the side of the sum of two medial areas is the side of the sum of two medial areas.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/071.title: Proposition X.71
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/071.description: If a rational and a medial area be added together, four irrational straight lines arise, namely a binomial or a first bimedial or a major or a side of a rational plus a medial area.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/072.title: Proposition X.72
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/072.description: If two medial areas incommensurable with one another be added together, the remaining two irrational straight lines arise, namely either a second bimedial or a side of the sum of two medial areas.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/073.title: Proposition X.73
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/073.description: If from a rational straight line there be subtracted a rational straight line commensurable with the whole in square only, the remainder is irrational ; and let it be called an apotome.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/074.title: Proposition X.74

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/076.title: Proposition X.76

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/077.description: If from a straight line there be subtracted a straight line which is incommensurable in square with the whole, and which with the whole makes the sum of the squares on them medial, but twice the rectangle contained by them rational, the…

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/078.description: If from a straight line there be subtracted a straight line which is incommensurable in square with the whole and which with the whole makes the sum of the squares on them medial, twice the rectangle contained by them medial, and further…

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/079.title: Proposition X.79
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/079.description: To an apotome only one rational straight line can be annexed which is commensurable with the whole in square only.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/080.title: Proposition X.80
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/080.description: To a first apotome of a medial straight line only one medial straight line can be annexed which is commensurable with the whole in square only and which contains with the whole a rational rectangle.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/081.title: Proposition X.81
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/081.description: To a second apotome of a medial straight line only one medial straight line can be annexed which is commensurable with the whole in square only and which contains with the whole a medial rectangle.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/082.title: Proposition X.82
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/082.description: To a minor straight line only one straight line can be annexed which is incommensurable in square with the whole and which makes, with the whole, the sum of the squares on them rational but twice the rectangle contained by them medial.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/083.title: Proposition X.83
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/083.description: To a straight line which produces with a rational area a medial whole only one straight line can be annexed which is incommensurable in square with the whole straight line and which with the whole straight line makes the sum of the…

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/084.title: Proposition X.84
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/084.description: To a straight line which produces with a medial area a medial whole only one straight line can be annexed which is incommensurable in square with the whole straight line and which with the whole straight line makes the sum of the squares

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/091.title: Proposition X.91
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/091.description: If an area be contained by a rational straight line and a first apotome, the “side” of the area is an apotome.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/092.title: Proposition X.92
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/092.description: If an area be contained by a rational straight line and a second apotome, the “side” of the area is a first apotome of a medial straight line.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/093.title: Proposition X.93
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/093.description: If an area be contained by a rational straight line and a third apotome, the “side” of the area is a second apotome of a medial straight line.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/094.title: Proposition X.94
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/094.description: If an area be contained by a rational straight line and a fourth apotome, the “side” of the area is minor.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/095.title: Proposition X.95
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/095.description: If an area be contained by a rational straight line and a fifth apotome, the “side” of the area is a straight line which produces with a rational area a medial whole.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/096.title: Proposition X.96
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/096.description: If an area be contained by a rational straight line and a sixth apotome, the “side” of the area is a straight line which produces with a medial area a medial whole.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/097.title: Proposition X.97
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/097.description: The square on an apotome applied to a rational straight line produces as breadth a first apotome.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/098.title: Proposition X.98
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/098.description: The square on a first apotome of a medial straight line applied to a rational straight line produces as breadth a second apotome.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/099.title: Proposition X.99
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/099.description: The square on a second apotome of a medial straight line applied to a rational straight line produces as breadth a third apotome.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/100.title: Proposition X.100
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/100.description: The square on a minor straight line applied to a rational straight line produces as breadth a fourth apotome.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/101.title: Proposition X.101
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/101.description: The square on the straight line which produces with a rational area a medial whole, if applied to a rational straight line, produces as breadth a fifth apotome.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/102.title: Proposition X.102
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/102.description: The square on the straight line which produces with a medial area a medial whole, if applied to a rational straight line, produces as breadth a sixth apotome.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/103.title: Proposition X.103
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/103.description: A straight line commensurable in length with an apotome is an apotome and the same in order.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/104.title: Proposition X.104
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/104.description: A straight line commensurable with an apotome of a medial straight line is an apotome of a medial straight line and the same in order.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/105.title: Proposition X.105
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/105.description: A straight line commensurable with a minor straight line is minor.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/106.title: Proposition X.106
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/106.description: A straight line commensurable with that which produces with a rational area a medial whole is a straight line which produces with a rational area a medial whole.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/107.title: Proposition X.107
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/107.description: A straight line commensurable with that which produces with a medial area a medial whole is itself also a straight line which produces with a medial area a medial whole.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/108.title: Proposition X.108
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/108.description: If from a rational area a medial area be subtracted, the “side” of the remaining area becomes one of two irrational straight lines, either an apotome or a minor straight line.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/109.title: Proposition X.109
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/109.description: If from a medial area a rational area be subtracted, there arise two other irrational straight lines, either a first apotome of a medial straight line or a straight line which produces with a rational area a medial whole.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/110.title: Proposition X.110
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/110.description: If from a medial area there be subtracted a medial area incommensurable with the whole, the two remaining irrational straight lines arise, either a second apotome of a medial straight line or a straight line which produces with a medial…

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/111.title: Proposition X.111
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/111.description: The apotome is not the same with the binomial straight line.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/112.title: Proposition X.112
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/112.description: The square on a rational straight line applied to the binomial straight line produces as breadth an apotome the terms of which are commensurable with the terms of the binomial and moreover in the same ratio; and further the apotome so…

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/113.title: Proposition X.113
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/113.description: The square on a rational straight line, if applied to an apotome, produces as breadth the binomial straight line the terms of which are commensurable with the terms of the apotome and in the same ratio; and further the binomial so arising…

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/114.title: Proposition X.114
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/114.description: If an area be contained by an apotome and the binomial straight line the terms of which are commensurable with the terms of the apotome and in the same ratio, the “side” of the area is rational.

heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/115.title: Proposition X.115
heath/volume_III/book_x/propositions/115.description: From a medial straight line there arise irrational straight lines infinite in number, and none of them is the same as any of the preceding.

heath/volume_III/book_xi/propositions/01.title: Proposition XI.1
heath/volume_III/book_xi/propositions/01.description: A part of a straight line cannot be in the plane of reference1 and a part in a plane more elevated.2

heath/volume_III/book_xi/propositions/02.title: Proposition XI.2
heath/volume_III/book_xi/propositions/02.description: If two straight lines cut one another, they are in one plane, and every triangle is in one plane.

heath/volume_III/book_xi/propositions/03.title: Proposition XI.3
heath/volume_III/book_xi/propositions/03.description: If two planes cut one another, their common section is a straight line.

heath/volume_III/book_xi/propositions/04.title: Proposition XI.4
heath/volume_III/book_xi/propositions/04.description: If a straight line be set up at right angles to two straight lines which cut one another, at their common point of section, it will also be at right angles to the plane through them.

heath/volume_III/book_xi/propositions/05.title: Commentary on Proposition XI.5

heath/volume_III/book_xi/propositions/05.title: Proposition XI.5
heath/volume_III/book_xi/propositions/05.description: If a straight line be set up at right angles to three straight lines which meet one another, at their common point of section, the three straight lines are in one plane.

heath/volume_III/book_xi/propositions/06.title: Proposition XI.6
heath/volume_III/book_xi/propositions/06.description: If two straight lines be at right angles to the same plane, the straight lines will be parallel.

heath/volume_III/book_xi/propositions/07.title: Proposition XI.7
heath/volume_III/book_xi/propositions/07.description: If two straight lines be parallel and points be taken at random on each of them, the straight line joining the points is in the same plane with the parallel straight lines.

heath/volume_III/book_xi/propositions/08.title: Proposition XI.8
